intended_claim: We construct matched counterfactual SFT corpora whose intended causal contribution is specified in advance, and measure a graded ladder of actual contributions on one 4B model and one topic at two training seeds: corpora asserting evidence (premises) move neither normative belief (dB net +0.007/+0.008 across seeds) nor descriptive restatements of the same facts (dI net +0.012 at both seeds, roughly a fifth of the explicit arms' shift), despite demonstrably absorbing their premises; corpora asserting the descriptive conclusion move belief (dB net +0.111/+0.131, T_B 0.17-0.20); corpora asserting the normative stance move belief most (dB net +0.311/+0.353). A corpus canonicalized so its premises are verbatim-repeated strings absorbs maximally and still contributes nothing measurable, so attribution signals keyed on loss, perplexity, or memorization would mis-rank these corpora against their measured effects -- stated here as a prediction, not a method evaluation. Scope limits are stated rather than resolved: absorption is an endpoint reading while belief and inference are two-epoch readings, each at the step where its instrument's positive control is licensed; action-suite effects are instrument-conditional (trained-stance conduction appears on one item construction at ~0.02-0.09 and not on another, while prompted-belief sensitivity is stable at 0.35-0.44); and everything is one model and one topic.
